# Command line reference

<!-- Generated by `go test ./cmd/hsmgate -run CLIReference -update` from what the commands print for -h: do not edit by hand. -->

One binary, several commands. This page is what `hsmgate <command> -h` prints. For what to do with them: [the README](../README.md), [operations.md](operations.md), [guides/clients.md](guides/clients.md).

## hsmgate

```text
hsmgate: a policy-checked door in front of a key token.

usage: hsmgate <command> [flags]       (hsmgate <command> -h shows the flags of a command)

  dev       start a throw-away service to try hsmgate: no hardware, nothing to prepare
  serve     run the service
  check     load a configuration, open the tokens and list every key version; starts nothing, needs no PIN
  unlock    give a card its PIN (to the running service, over its admin socket)
  encrypt   seal a value (or the files of a directory) with a key of the service
  decrypt   open what encrypt sealed
  ca        make the certificates: the authority, the service, the clients (init, setup, server, client, list)
  ping      connect to the listener (a container health check; a TCP connect, or the whole TLS handshake with a certificate that has no rights)
  version   print the version

Documentation: https://github.com/zystem/hsmgate#readme
```

## hsmgate dev

Try it in a minute (see the README). Everything it makes is deleted when it stops, unless `-dir` is given.

```text
usage: hsmgate dev [-listen 127.0.0.1:8443] [-dir DIR]

A throw-away service to try hsmgate in a minute, with no hardware and no files to prepare: a software token with a fresh key, a CA of its own, the certificate of the
service and of one client (demo), and the keys "demo" (no context) and "demo-ctx" (the context must begin with "demo/"). It prints what to type to use it.
NOT for real keys: the key is a file, and without -dir everything is deleted when the service stops (what it sealed can never be opened again).
-dir DIR keeps the files there (the directory must be new or empty) and, run again on the same directory, starts the same service with the same key and address.

  -dir string
    	keep the files in this new or empty directory (default: a temporary one, deleted at the stop)
  -listen string
    	address to listen on (loopback unless you say otherwise) (default "127.0.0.1:8443")
```

## hsmgate serve

```text
usage: hsmgate serve -config hsmgate.yaml

Runs the service until SIGINT or SIGTERM (then the tokens are logged out). SIGHUP reloads the configuration, the policy and the certificates.

  -config string
    	configuration file (default "hsmgate.yaml")
```

## hsmgate check

```text
usage: hsmgate check -config hsmgate.yaml

Loads the configuration, opens the tokens and prints every key version with its holders, their state and the fingerprint of the public key. Starts nothing and needs no PIN. Exit status 0 means the configuration is good.

  -config string
    	configuration file (default "hsmgate.yaml")
```

## hsmgate unlock

```text
usage: hsmgate unlock -config hsmgate.yaml -token NAME [-pin-stdin]

Hands the PIN of a card to the running service over its admin socket (admin_socket of the configuration). The PIN is read from the terminal without echo, or from standard input with -pin-stdin; it is never an argument and stays in memory only.

  -config string
    	configuration file (default "hsmgate.yaml")
  -pin-stdin
    	read the PIN from standard input instead of the terminal
  -token string
    	the token to unlock (a name in tokens: of the configuration)
```

## hsmgate encrypt

Environment variables stand in for the flags `-addr`, `-ca`, `-cert`, `-keyfile`, `-transit-key`, `-mount` (as `HSMGATE_ADDR`, ...). Several values at once, and Kubernetes Secrets: `-in-dir`, `-in-files`, `-k8s`.

```text
Usage of encrypt:
  -addr string
    	address of the service, https://host:8443 (env HSMGATE_ADDR)
  -ca string
    	CA certificate of the service, PEM (env HSMGATE_CA)
  -cert string
    	client certificate, PEM (env HSMGATE_CERT)
  -context string
    	context of the single value (-in/-out)
  -context-prefix string
    	for -in-dir and -in-files: the context of a value is this prefix followed by the name of the ciphertext file, e.g. k8s/$(POD_NAMESPACE)/app-secrets/
  -in string
    	one file with a value, or - for standard input (default "-")
  -in-dir string
    	a directory: every regular file in it (not those starting with a dot) is a value
  -in-files value
    	files with a value, a comma-separated list (the flag may be repeated)
  -k8s string
    	NAMESPACE/SECRET/FIELD for one value, NAMESPACE/SECRET for -in-dir and -in-files: sets the context (k8s/NAMESPACE/SECRET/FIELD) and prints a Kubernetes Secret manifest instead of ciphertext files
  -keyfile string
    	private key of the client certificate, PEM (env HSMGATE_KEYFILE)
  -mode string
    	permission bits (octal) of the files that are written (default "0644")
  -mount string
    	Transit mount (env HSMGATE_MOUNT) (default "transit")
  -out string
    	where its ciphertext goes for -in: a file, or - for standard output (default "-")
  -out-dir string
    	a directory for its ciphertext of -in-dir: a file of the same name each; also the default place for -in-files
  -out-files value
    	where its ciphertext of -in-files goes: a comma-separated list as long as -in-files, by position; a different length is refused
  -raw
    	keep a trailing newline of the input (by default one is removed)
  -transit-key string
    	name of the key in the service (env HSMGATE_TRANSIT_KEY)
  -wait duration
    	how long to try again when the service says it may pass (locked token, busy, rate) (default 1m0s)
```

## hsmgate decrypt

```text
Usage of decrypt:
  -addr string
    	address of the service, https://host:8443 (env HSMGATE_ADDR)
  -ca string
    	CA certificate of the service, PEM (env HSMGATE_CA)
  -cert string
    	client certificate, PEM (env HSMGATE_CERT)
  -context string
    	context of the single value (-in/-out)
  -context-prefix string
    	for -in-dir and -in-files: the context of a value is this prefix followed by the name of the ciphertext file, e.g. k8s/$(POD_NAMESPACE)/app-secrets/
  -in string
    	one file with a ciphertext, or - for standard input (default "-")
  -in-dir string
    	a directory: every regular file in it (not those starting with a dot) is a ciphertext
  -in-files value
    	files with a ciphertext, a comma-separated list (the flag may be repeated)
  -keyfile string
    	private key of the client certificate, PEM (env HSMGATE_KEYFILE)
  -mode string
    	permission bits (octal) of the files that are written (default "0440")
  -mount string
    	Transit mount (env HSMGATE_MOUNT) (default "transit")
  -out string
    	where the value goes for -in: a file, or - for standard output (default "-")
  -out-dir string
    	a directory for the value of -in-dir: a file of the same name each; also the default place for -in-files
  -out-files value
    	where the value of -in-files goes: a comma-separated list as long as -in-files, by position; a different length is refused
  -transit-key string
    	name of the key in the service (env HSMGATE_TRANSIT_KEY)
  -wait duration
    	how long to try again when the service says it may pass (locked token, busy, rate) (default 1m0s)
```

## hsmgate ca

The commands that make certificates. `hsmgate ca` alone prints this; the flags below are shared by `setup`, `init`, `server`, `client` and `list` (each uses the ones its line above names).

```text
usage:
  hsmgate ca setup  -config hsmgate.yaml [-client NAME[,NAME]]      everything in one command: the authority, the server certificate (written where tls: of the
                                                                    configuration says, its names guessed from listen: and the interfaces) and client certificates
  hsmgate ca init   -dir DIR [-name "hsmgate CA"] [-days 3650] [-mode file|sealed|token -config hsmgate.yaml -token NAME -label LABEL]
  hsmgate ca server -dir DIR (-config hsmgate.yaml | -out DIR) [-dns NAME[,NAME]] [-ip ADDR[,ADDR]] [-cn NAME] [-days 365] [-owner USER]
  hsmgate ca client -dir DIR (-config hsmgate.yaml | -out DIR) -cn NAME [-uri URI] [-days 365] [-owner USER]
  hsmgate ca list   -dir DIR
the key of the authority: -mode file (the default: ca.key in DIR, a secret), sealed (sealed to the ECDH key LABEL of the token: nothing secret in DIR, the token opens it when a
certificate is issued), token (the signing key LABEL of the token makes the signatures: the key exists nowhere else). Commands that issue need -config (and the PIN, asked
for on the terminal or with -pin-stdin) when the key is on or sealed to a token. With -config the names of the server certificate, the paths and the owner of the key file are
guessed when they are not given; the commands say what they guessed.
```

## hsmgate ca: the flags

```text
Usage of ca setup:
  -client string
    	setup: names of clients to make certificates for, comma separated
  -cn string
    	the common name (a client: its identity in the policy)
  -config string
    	the configuration of the service (the token, the tls paths, listen)
  -days int
    	life in days (the authority: 3650, a certificate: 365)
  -dir string
    	the directory of the authority (with -config: ca/ next to the configuration)
  -dns string
    	server: DNS names, comma separated (guessed with -config)
  -ip string
    	server: IP addresses, comma separated (guessed with -config)
  -label string
    	init, setup: the label of the token's key (ECDH key for sealed, signing key for token)
  -mode string
    	init, setup: where the key of the authority is: file, sealed or token (default "file")
  -name string
    	init, setup: the name of the authority (default "hsmgate CA")
  -out string
    	server, client: the directory to write the certificate and key to (with -config: where tls: names, and clients/ next to the configuration)
  -owner string
    	server, client: the user that owns the key file (default: hsmgate, if it exists and this runs as root)
  -pin-stdin
    	read the PIN of the token from standard input instead of the terminal
  -token string
    	the token of the configuration (default: the one the authority was made with)
  -uri string
    	client: URI names, comma separated (a SPIFFE id for example)
```

## hsmgate ping

```text
usage: hsmgate ping [-addr host:port] [-cert file -key file -ca file [-name server-name]]

Connects to the listener and exits 0 when it answers: a health check (a container, a Kubernetes probe) that never touches a token. Without -cert it is a TCP connect and needs no certificate. With -cert, -key and -ca it makes the whole TLS 1.3 handshake (the certificate of the service checked against the CA, a client certificate shown) and sends no request: use a certificate of the CA that no entry of clients: names, so that the probe has no rights and leaves no audit line.

  -addr string
    	address to connect to (default "127.0.0.1:8443")
  -ca string
    	TLS mode: the CA that signed the certificate of the service
  -cert string
    	TLS mode: the certificate of the probe (a certificate of the CA that no client of the policy uses)
  -key string
    	TLS mode: the key of that certificate
  -name string
    	TLS mode: the name the certificate of the service must carry (default: the host of -addr)
  -timeout duration
    	give up after this long (default 3s)
```

## hsmgate version

Prints the version (`hsmgate v0.7.3`; `hsmgate dev` for a build from a clone).
